text:
Alice Chen: Heads-up — after toggling FP8 on the H100 fleet (L40S configs mirrored) we're seeing a ~2.3x latency spike on long-history chat workloads and occasional KV-cache memory churn. Repro on Canary A.
Marco Ruiz: Can you paste the kernel selection log from the runtime? curious if we're falling back to a slower kernel or doing FP16 emulation.
Alice Chen: Copying relevant snippet:```
kernel_selector: selected_kernel=te_fp8_intkern_v2
fallbacks: none
peformance_estimate: 0.38ms/token (expected ~0.15ms)
notes: AMP fallback triggered for layer 13 due to infs during calibration
```
Priya Kapoor: AMP fallback + "infs during calibration" sounds like numeric stability during per-layer calibrate. Did the calibration pass finish normally or did we abort and reuse older scales?
Alice Chen: Calibration job finished but with warnings: ``[WARN] layer_13: scale_exceeded_count=4, nan_count=2``. The runtime marked the layer as "unsafe" and inserted an FP32 path for that layer which seems to blow up scheduling.
Jamal Thompson: When runtime inserts FP32 path it disables TensorEngine fused kernels for that layer — that can increase memory bandwidth and invalidates batch scheduling heuristics. That matches 2-3x latency regression.
Marco Ruiz: Can you grab perf counters + kv cache stats from the same run? I want to see cache misses and hot eviction rates.
Alice Chen: kv stats (canary A): ``kv_cache_size=24GB, max_live_entries=9.8M, evict_rate=0.72/s, avg_lookup_latency=0.74ms``. Before FP8 we had evict_rate=0.04/s and avg_lookup_latency=0.12ms.
Priya Kapoor: Wow, that's a huge difference. Why would FP8 change KV behaviour? Could be side-effect of different kernel tiling increasing working set per request, causing more memory pressure on GPU L2 and forcing evictions.
Marco Ruiz: Also check per-request token-batch packing. If per-layer FP32 fallbacks add memory/headroom variance, our continuous batching may stop coalescing requests leading to smaller effective batches. That hurts throughput.
Alice Chen: I attached a profiling flame (summary): p95_latency=310ms (prev 130ms), tokens_per_second=6.4k (prev 14.8k), kernel_time_share: transform_kern=64%, memcpy=18%, kernel_launch_overhead=10%.
Jamal Thompson: The memcpy % suggests extra host<->device traffic or more fragmented device memory use. Any change in allocator flags or prefetching?
Alice Chen: We didn't change allocator but FP8 codepath enables TE prefetch for KV by default. I tried toggling TE_PREFETCH=0 and reran: p95 dropped to 190ms, tokens/sec up to 9.9k, but still worse than baseline.
Priya Kapoor: That indicates multiple contributors: prefetch interaction + FP32 fallback layers. Two-prong approach: 1) Make calibration less aggressive (increase clip threshold / reduce scale growth) so fewer fallbacks. 2) Improve kernel selection to prefer a mixed-precision kernel that can accept occasional NaNs and correct post-hoc rather than forcing full FP32 fallback.
Marco Ruiz: For (1) we can change env: FP8_CALIB_MODE=stable, FP8_CLIP=1e-3 and re-run. For (2) propose a new heuristic: allow TE_fp8_mixed kernel when layer inf_count < 10 and enable per-iteration clamp instead of full fallback. We'll need an experiment.
Alice Chen: Running with FP8_CALIB_MODE=stable now. Quick probing run shows inf_count decreased to 0, scale adjustments smaller. p95=145ms — much closer.
deploy-bot: Canary A deploy v2.14.3 started by Alice Chen.
Marco Ruiz: Good. We also need to update kernel_selector logs to more clearly show "soft-fallback" vs "hard-fallback". Right now both are collapsed and it's impossible to tell if kernel did in-place clamp or switched execution precision.
Jamal Thompson: Agreed — add markers to trace: `kernel=te_fp8_mixed [soft-fallback:clamp]` vs `kernel=fp32_path [hard-fallback]`. That will help SLO triage.
Priya Kapoor: Also noticing that L40S had slightly different transformer-engine defaults (autocast thresholds). On L40S increase of per-layer workspace size triggered earlier fallback. We should align TE configs across H100/L40S for FP8 path or at least ship platform-aware defaults.
Alice Chen: Action items I captured: 1) PR to runtime: expose FP8_CALIB_MODE and FP8_CLIP; 2) PR to kernel_selector: emit soft vs hard fallback; 3) Experiment: enable te_fp8_mixed with per-iter clamp for 24h; 4) Telemetry: add kv_cache eviction & memcpy% to perf dashboard.
Marco Ruiz: I'll own (2) and (3). Priya you take (1) telemetry piece?
Priya Kapoor: Taking telemetry and will add dashboard tiles with historical baselines.
Jamal Thompson: I'll run a stress suite across both H100 and L40S sims with the new envs to confirm regressions are closed under mixed traffic.
Alice Chen: Thanks team. If anyone hits this on staging, DM me. For now, holding FP8 rollout to Dedicated until we have soft-fallback kernel and stable calibration settings. :thumbsup:
infra-bot: Note: Canary A was rolled back to v2.14.2 by automation due to sustained p95 > 250ms for 10m.
